headline: Composition and asymmetry tune condensate ageing, organization and electrostatics
label: Biomolecular Condensate Modeling
summary: Residue-resolved and coarse-grained simulations now link condensate ageing, organization and electric potentials to sequence composition and binding partners.
synthesis: The three preprints share a focus on how sequence composition and molecular context govern biomolecular condensate behavior, studied with molecular dynamics. Residue-resolved simulations of FUS show that RNA and heterotypic protein interactions tune LARKS contacts and cross-beta-sheet formation, which govern condensate ageing. A coarse-grained stickers-and-spacers model with directional sticker interactions reports that spacer heterogeneity boosts condensation while trading off against organization. A third study shows that molecular asymmetry in cation and anion affinities, together with chain-terminus placement, sets electric potential profiles within condensates. What is new is the explicit mapping of condensate properties, including ageing, organization and electrostatics, onto specific molecular features such as sequence asymmetry, spacer design and binding partners.
